items.label: E1
items.text: Ladders are permitted in the orchard only when a second worker holds the base of the ladder.

items.label: E2
items.text: Ladders are not permitted in the orchard overnight and must be returned to the tool shed.

items.label: E3
items.text:
Saplings in the fixture orchard are planted between the third and fifth week of the planting season. Each sapling receives 12 litres of water on the day it is planted.

Approved sapling varieties:

1. Red Fixture Apple

2. Golden Fixture Pear

3. Blue Fixture Plum

items.label: E4
items.text: Wicks are trimmed to a height of 4 millimetres. A wick trimmed too short produces a dim beam; a wick left too long produces soot on the lens.

items.label: E5
items.text: The keeper polishes the lens with a dry chamois cloth. Abrasive powders are not permitted on the lens.

items.label: E6
items.text:
Before leaving the shed, each worker must:
1. Clean the blades.
2. Hang every tool on its hook.
3. Sign the tool register.

items.label: E7
items.text:
TEST FIXTURE ONLY. Synthetic text written for software tests; it is not part of any real corpus.

The fixture observatory opens its dome only when the wind speed is below 25 kilometres per hour. Observers log the dome status every hour.

The main telescope is recalibrated on the first night of every month. Calibration takes about ninety minutes and is recorded in the calibration journal.

Visitors are welcome on Fridays. Visitors may not touch the telescope controls.

items.label: E8
items.text: The lamp of the fixture lighthouse must be cleaned every evening before sunset. Keepers record each cleaning in the lamp register.
